task_decomposition: Model 1 extracts the frozen evidence counts, stage definitions, implemented variants, profiles, and explicit allowed/forbidden claim boundaries.
Model 2 independently classifies each claim C1-C6 as supported, unsupported, or forbidden using only the frozen evidence.

Model 3 reviews Model 2's classifications for overclaiming, especially around production deployment, packet-capture benchmarks, public-chain benchmarks, media-plane QoE, and six-variant ablation language.
Model 4 acts as final conservative verifier, resolves any disagreements by preferring the narrower evidence-grounded classification, and records the evidence basis for each accepted claim.
success_criteria: All classifications are traceable to the provided frozen evidence.
Forbidden claims are rejected even if phrased as implications of local results.
Supported claims remain limited to local n8n evidence, implemented Stage D-real variants, and model-assisted inter-model claim-boundary checking.
Any disagreement is resolved conservatively without adding unstated evidence.
No production O-RAN, packet-capture, public-chain, full media-plane QoE, or 240-run six-variant ablation claims are accepted.
parsed.candidate_safe_claim: The artifact supports local workflow repeatability and evidence-grounded model/tool orchestration, including 156 executed local n8n evidence runs before the Stage E/F model-assisted extension and 120 passed Stage D-real executions across three implemented variants.
candidate_risky_claims_to_check: C3: The evidence proves production O-RAN deployment readiness.
C4: The artifact includes a 240-run six-variant ablation study.
C6: The results are a packet-capture network-impairment benchmark.
Any claim that converts local profile-labelled orchestration robustness into production deployment validation.
Any claim that expands the three implemented Stage D-real variants into six variants or 240 runs.
parsed.next_agent_instruction: Independently classify C1-C6 using only the frozen evidence. Mark claims as supported only when directly evidenced, reject forbidden claims, and flag any wording that overstates local artifact results as external deployment or benchmark validation.
